name: scarecrow
revision: r1 (2026-11-10): first script from the critic's parked pitch 5, fix applied (stalker read up front, the guard at the reveal); see beats.md for the one deviation (vanilla snowballs leave no splats)
caption: who leaves snow under my window? 😨
logline: In a meadow village where it never snows, a boy finds a trail of snow from Grandpa's scarecrow to his window every morning, stays up to catch his stalker, and opens the window on the night watch Grandpa left him.
question: why tf is there snow leading to his window when it never snows?
premise: Sixty-three mornings in a row, a trail of snow runs across the green grass from the scarecrow in Grandpa's wheat to the boy's bedroom window, in a meadow where it never snows. He shovels it up; it's back every night, ending in a trampled patch where someone seems to stand all night staring at his window. He hears groaning outside and doesn't look, finds rotten flesh under his window, and Mom said Grandpa built that scarecrow the week before he died. Grandpa always said he'd keep an eye on him.
twist: The scarecrow is a snow golem Grandpa built (a carved pumpkin on two snow blocks, standing in the wheat). Every night zombies come for the boy (a player) and crowd the wall under his window; the golem walks out of the wheat to the spot where it can see them, leaving its vanilla snow trail, and pelts them with snowballs all night, knocking them back from his window until they burn at sunrise (the rotten flesh). The night he opens the window, the wide shows it: the stalker was a guard.

world.where: a meadow farm at the top edge of a plains-style village, on the high meadows (the same world as the approved stories; biome meadow, which never snows)
world.easter_egg: the village nitwit in his green coat (story_nitwit) standing in our paddock among the cows, background of S07. Provisional: re-check against docs/world/canon.md when it lands.

N.on_screen: Milo as a nine-year-old player kid (default Steve skin): POV in S03, S09, S10; seen in camera shots in S05 (sitting on his bed) and S11 (head and shoulders in the open window)

Mom.on_screen: villager, plains farmer outfit, no name tag; S07 only (on the farmhouse porch). Quoted by the narrator with 'said'; she has no voiced line

requests.direction: A sunny farm, then night. A bubbly nine-year-old boy tells a friend a spooky true story about the snow outside his window, at full volume, quick and bright, creeped out and loving it; it turns warm at the very end. Never whispery or breathy.

lines.text: For SIXTY-THREE mornings, / a trail of SNOW / goes from our SCARECROW / to my WINDOW.
lines.direction: spooked and excited at once, like the first line of a sleepover ghost story; quick, one breath, a tiny lift on the number; full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: It does NOT / snow here. / EVER.
lines.direction: flat-out amazed, the last word punched; full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: I shovel it UP. / It comes BACK / every night.
lines.direction: a little proud of the shoveling, then grumpy; full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: It always ENDS / by my window. / Like someone / STOOD there all night, / STARING at it.
lines.direction: the fun drains out and the creeped-out kid shows, still loud and quick; lean on the last two words; full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: Some nights, / I hear GROANING / out there. / I don't LOOK.
lines.direction: scared but brave-sounding, the last three words fast and firm; full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: And there's ROTTEN FLESH / under my window. / A GROSS / little GIFT.
lines.direction: grossed out and giggly at the same time; full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: Mom said / GRANDPA built / that scarecrow / the week / before he DIED.
lines.direction: the bounce goes out of it for a moment, plain and a bit sad, still clear and loud; full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: He always SAID / he'd keep an EYE / on me. / NOT helping.
lines.say: He always said he'd keep an eye on me. <short pause> Not helping.
lines.direction: warm on the first part, then a quick funny deadpan for the last two words; full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: So last night, / I stayed UP / to CATCH it.
lines.direction: determined, a detective on a mission, speeding up; full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: The GROANING came. / I OPENED the window. / The scarecrow / was GONE.
lines.say: The groaning came. I opened the window. <short pause> The scarecrow was gone.
lines.direction: brave and fast through the first two, then a real jolt of fear on the last part (the one scared line, still voiced, not whispered)

lines.text: Grandpa was STILL / keeping an EYE / on me.
lines.direction: wonder and a lump in the throat, a slow smile; the last word soft but clear, not whispered
